Get the interface. Tessellate turns product intent into cohesive interface systems using an open library of components, patterns, motion and design intelligence. PRESET EXEMPLARS: AI research terminal luxury travel marketplace playful HR platform developer observability tool minimalist finance app PRODUCT BRIEF Deterministic Core Active FEEL AMBITION 60 / 100 STRUCTURE 50 / 100 STACK React 19 + Tailwind CSS 4 Compose CURRENT SETTINGS Visual ambition 60 / 100 Structural creativity 50 / 100 These are your selected values. Compose carries them with the brief into the deterministic product pipeline. THREE DIRECTIONS, ONE PRODUCT Choose a direction. Or blend them. Generate an employee experience example with the real catalogue and composer. Compare its sidebar, editorial and rail workspace structures, then edit the exact project in Workbench. Generate example directionsCompose your own brief THE COMPOSITION PARADIGM Not a component library. A composition system. A resource catalogue gives you reusable building blocks. Tessellate adds a product brief, shared design settings, and a manifest that connects screens, resources, and project intent. Starting from a Resource Catalogue Choose resources: The product team decides which components belong on each screen. Carry design decisions: Shared tokens and interaction patterns need to stay aligned across resources. Connect the screens: The team defines navigation, content, and how interface parts work together. Review generated code: Check markup, styles, and behavior in the context of the product. Outcome: Resource choice, integration, and consistency rem

metrics.title: Privacy in this review — Tessellate
metrics.bodyText: Skip to content Tessellate Explore Showcases Compose Workbench Tools Agents Creators Docs Search ⌘K Local projects Start building OPEN INTERFACE COMMONS Privacy in this review A factual description of the current guest and browser storage boundary. Local project storage Project manifests, edits, checkpoints and saved resource collections use browser storage on this origin. Export your project to retain a portable copy. Clearing browser site data removes local records. Credentials Core browsing, composition, editing and export need no provider key. BYO provider credentials must remain ephemeral and are never written to project manifests, D1 or R2. Hosting ChatGPT Sites serves the site and receives ordinary page and asset requests. Review the hosting provider privacy policy for its processing. Tessellate does not add third-party analytics, advertise fabricated usage counts or provision an additional database for this review. Public previews Resource previews use sandboxed frames without same-origin privileges. Treat all example content as synthetic demonstration data, not real employee records. metrics.bodyText: Skip to content Tessellate Search ⌘K Build ← Back to Documentation Design DNA & Manifest Contracts Tessellate rejects arbitrary visual hallucination. Every screen is an Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) governed by canonical schemas. The 12 Dimensions of Design DNA Every interface system in Tessellate is defined along 12 continuous normalized axes (0–100): dataDensity (0–100) trust (0–100) interactionDensity (0–100) visualAmbition (0–100) motion (0–100) typographicExpression (0–100) imageryIntensity (0–100) depth (0–100) colorSaturation (0–100) radiusScale (0–100) borderWeight (0–100) contrastFloor (0–100) Canonical Package Schemas Import Zod contracts directly into your TypeScript projects: import { ResourceManifestSchema, ProjectManifestSchema, DesignDNASchema, ScreenNodeSchema } from '@tessellate/schemas'; Start with a product brief. No credit card. No account required. Runs locally in your browser.
